case_text:
Vignette:
A 22-year-old sexually active man presents with a 4-day history of gradually worsening left scrotal pain and swelling. The pain is dull and aching and radiates to the left inguinal region. He reports mild dysuria and a small amount of urethral discharge noticed over the past week. He has had a new sexual partner in the past month and inconsistently uses barrier protection. He denies fever, nausea, vomiting, or testicular trauma. Vital signs are normal. On examination, the left hemiscrotum is swollen and erythematous. There is tenderness and induration localized to the left epididymis posterior to the testis. Prehn sign is positive with relief of pain on elevation of the left testis. The cremasteric reflex is present bilaterally. There is no testicular torsion on clinical assessment. Urinalysis shows 15 to 20 WBC per high-power field. A nucleic acid amplification test for chlamydia and gonorrhea is sent.
